before: A tag measured its label with a thin space on each side as its only padding, and paint then drew a transparent gap inside that measured width. The label was wider than the room left for it, so the centred text overflowed and the browser aligned it to the start: the left side of a chip had padding and the right side none, worst on a one-glyph chip.
after: The room around a tag's label is geometry: a transparent gap between neighbours and a padding inside the fill, both on each side. Every place that measures a piece adds it to the label's measured width, and paint draws exactly it, so the label is centred with the same room on both sides.
reason: Tags are view-only layout pieces: nothing changes in the document, in the store or in any shared update. Only the advance a tag takes on a laid-out line grows.
